paper.title: Complex Contagions and the Weakness of Long Ties

headline: agent-based reproduction: 3/3 locked clauses REPRO; R=1 adoption(p=1)=1.000 vs (p=0)=1.000; R=2 adoption(p=0)=1.000 vs (p=1)=0.006; crossover present

verdicts.gate: P1 simple (R=1): adoption(p=1) >= adoption(p=0) (randomization does not hurt)
P2 complex (R=2): adoption(p=0) > adoption(p=1) (clustering helps; long ties weak)
P3 crossover: sign[adoption(p=1)-adoption(p=0)] flips between R=1 and R=2

extra.scope: faithful reproduction of a published synthetic model; no real-world data; outcome = final adoption fraction at a fixed point; the contribution is whether the harness + lock-before-run discipline reproduce the landmark complex-contagion result.

citations: Centola, D. & Macy, M. (2007). Complex Contagions and the Weakness of Long Ties. American Journal of Sociology 113(3):702-734. doi:10.1086/521848.
Centola, D., Eguiluz, V.M. & Macy, M. (2007). Cascade dynamics of complex propagation. Physica A 374:449-456. https://ndg.asc.upenn.edu/wp-content/uploads/2016/04/Centola-et-al-2007-PA.pdf

benchmark.note: no cross-tool baseline; faithful reproduction of a published model
